ledger.note: 1989: the Wa State begins on 17 April. 'On 17 April 1989, Bao Youxiang's forces announced their separation from the Communist Party of Burma' (infobox: UWSP and UWSA formed 17 April 1989); the capital is Pangkham. The page gives the area, not a boundary.

region.text: the 13,000 km2 southern region bordering Thailand ('the Mong Yawn valley'): a 75 km circle at Mong Hsat cut to Shan State; the Wa State page names no coordinates

ledger.note: 1996: the Wa move into the Thai-border country of the Mong Tai Army. The MTA page says the UWSA 'managed to occupy two large swathes of territory near the Thai border' (undated; the MTA fought the UWSA until 1996); the Wa State page gives two accounts of the south ('by force' in the 1990s; 'granted in 1989') and dates the resettlement 1999-2002. Year and place are a bridging judgment (page silent).

notes: Rebel (de facto autonomous) state added by se-04-x; Myanmar's 2008 constitution recognises the northern part as the Wa Self-Administered Division of Shan State (created 20 August 2010, Wa page infobox), which the researcher left as a status note rather than a ledger event. Counterparts: communist-party-of-burma (written here), mong-tai-army (written here), union-of-burma (no matching events there). The circles are the researcher's placements: the Wa State page gives areas (27,000 body, 30,000 infobox, 13,000 south) and the names Pangkham, Mong Pawk, Mongmao, Wan Hoong, Mong Yawn, but no coordinates except the capital's; the southern area is placed at Mong Hsat on a bridging judgment because the Mong Hsat page does not mention the Wa. Hopang is the Myanmar government's assigned capital of the Division (Pangkham page). The two Wa State accounts of the south and the ceasefire date (9 May infobox, 18 May text) disagree. Gazetteer names wanted: Pangkham, Hopang, Mong Pawk, Mong Yawn (places). Page budget: 6 pages including coordinate pages.
